facts.text: Romano-British religion, not game canon: Coventina was the goddess of a sacred spring, with a shrine at Carrawburgh on Hadrian's Wall.
The priestesses washing the king's chamber and their order's coming to the barrows are Living Server writing.

story:
Coventina was a goddess of springs in Rome's day, and her shrines stood along the Wall, where soldiers threw coins into her water and asked her to keep them whole. Her priestesses kept the water pure. When the legions went home most of her shrines were filled in, and her order went where clean water was still needed. Two of them came to the barrows under the great circle.

They keep a well in the west halls, two women in white side by side, never apart, and they draw its water and pour it on the floor, and the floor takes it; and directly underneath, where the water goes, is the chamber where Uther Pendragon was laid, and his shade walks it. They say they keep the king's chamber washed. They will not say whether they wash it for the king's sake, or to keep what is in it from rising further.

They are not dead. Nobody knows what they are, after so long. The Church of Camelot calls them heathen; the druids of the Plains say they are the only ones in the barrows still doing what they were put there to do. They answer each other without speaking, and when one turns, both turn.
legend: Two Priestesses of Purity, level 44, stand side by side by the well in the upper west halls of the Barrows, right above Uther's chamber. Same faction (Coventina) and a step apart, so you always get both. No spells in the data, just melee. Mez one, kill the other. Their spot is a quick way to get noticed by everything around the Pendragon hall, so fight them where they stand.

aggro: The well is not for you.

lairEntry: Two women in white keep a well over a king.
